title: Colts' defense has already given up more than 1,000 yards
description: As the 0-2 Colts prepare for an AFC South showdown with the 0-2 Texans, Indy needs to hope for something better from the defense.
fullText:
As the 0-2 Colts prepare for an AFC South showdown with the 0-2 Texans, Indy needs to hope for something better from the defense.

Through two games, the Colts have surrendered more than 1,029 yards. The Ravens gained 506 yards against the Colts in Week 1, and the Chiefs added 523 yards in Week 2

Via NBC Sports research, the Colts would become only the second team in the Super Bowl era to give up 500 or more yards in three consecutive games, if it happens again on Sunday.

The 2018 Bengals are the only team to give up 500 or more yards in three straight games.

The Colts have also lost four straight AFC South games, their longest streak of division losses since the division was created in 2002. And the Colts have lost nine in a row, the longest active streak in the NFL.

title: Rams announce 2 practice squad elevations for Sunday vs. Broncos
description: The Rams have promoted 2 players from the practice squad this week, including a preseason darling at RB.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams are bringing two practice squad players with them to Denver for Sunday night's game against the Broncos. The team announced on Saturday that it has elevated running back Dean Connors and linebacker Elias Neal from the practice squad.

Connors gets the promotion after the Rams placed Ronnie Rivers on injured reserve. Sean McVay said that Connors will only get snaps on offense if an injury to Kyren Williams or Blake Corum occurs, so he'll contribute on special teams first and foremost.

Connors was a preseason standout for the Rams, and though he came up short of making the 53-man roster, he did earn a spot on the practice squad and now gets to suit up on game day, provided he's active.

Neal adds depth at linebacker and he will also help on special teams. This is his second elevation this season, so he can only be elevated one more time before hitting the limit for the season. After that, the Rams will need to sign him to the active roster if they want him to play in games.

The Rams and Broncos square off on Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET.

title: Delaware at Virginia football live updates, score, analysis, TV info
description: Recently ranked Virginia a tough test for the Blue Hens in their final nonconference game.
fullText:
CHARLOTTESVILLE, Virginia – Three years ago, Delaware traveled to State College to take on Penn State, the nation's seventh-ranked team.

The 2026 Blue Hens are set to face what is likely Delaware's toughest foe since then today.

Penn State routed the Blue Hens, who were then an FCS-level team, 63-7 that afternoon. Now in their second season at the FBS level, Delaware expects to be much more competitive than that against Virginia. But it remains an immense challenge for the 2-1 Blue Hens.

Kickoff is at 6 p.m. and the ACC Network is televising the game. The weather is sunny and clear as kickoff approaches.

HOW TO WATCH: Delaware visits ACC power Virginia in football

Ironically, Virginia's quarterback will be Beau Pribula, who saw duty for Penn State in that 2023 game against Delaware. The Blue Hens will get after him with a defense that ranks 10th nationally with 3.33 sacks per game.

The Cavaliers have improved significantly of late. Last year, they won the ACC regular-season title, lost in the conference title game to Duke and finished 11-3 and 16th in the national rankings.

This year they are 2-1 and had been ranked 25th nationally before last week's loss to West Virginia. So Virginia will be a significant task for the Blue Hens, yet one they'll welcome in their final nonconference game before Conference USA play commences.

"I'm glad we're kind of continuing to test ourselves," coach Ryan Carty said, "and kind of see who we are and get a feel for what we are as a team and how we play together … prior to getting into conference play."

Two weeks ago in its first game against an SEC foe, Delaware led at halftime at Vanderbilt before losing 35-26.

"That Vandy game, that's a great opponent right there and that game showed our toughness as a defense, and that we're willing to stay in close games and in a dogfight, and that we're not going to back down," Delaware cornerback Jamarion Kolagbodi said. "We're going to go toe to toe with anybody."

Virginia looms as a likely tougher test, as Carty raved about a Cavaliers defense that is quite adept at forcing turnovers. Delaware ranks 11th nationally, averaging 325.7 passing yards per game.

"We have to make sure that we protect the football," he said. "We gotta stop the run on defense, and I think we have to be able to run the ball on offense. We have to be able to limit our third and longs."

It also will be an emotional day for home fans, as this is Virginia's annual UVA Strong Day, when they honor the three football players who died in a 2022 on-campus shooting.

title: Broncos defense got back on track in Week 2, but real test comes vs. Rams
description: It’s been a tale of two weeks for both the Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Rams so far in 2026, and now the two collide in Week 3 with both looking to get above .500 for the first time on the young season. The Rams were humiliated in prime time to open the season in Australia, falling to the 49ers 27-7 in a lifeless performance that was surely […] The post Broncos defense got back on track in Week 2, but real test comes vs. Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Broncos defense got back on track in Week 2, but real test comes vs. Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

It's been a tale of two weeks for both the Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Rams so far in 2026, and now the two collide in Week 3 with both looking to get above .500 for the first time on the young season.

The Rams were humiliated in prime time to open the season in Australia, falling to the 49ers 27-7 in a lifeless performance that was surely affected by their bizarre travel plans. In Week 2, they responded with a dominant 28-6 drubbing of the New York Giants on Monday night to get back to 1-1. Now, it will be a third consecutive prime time game for Sean McVay and company.

The Broncos also took one on the chin in front of the whole nation in Week 1 at the hands of a bitter division rival. But it was how Sean Payton and company responded from that 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, with a 20-13 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars, that has fans feeling good heading into the rest of the season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The story of that turnaround from Week 1 to Week 2 was the Denver defense. Kenneth Walker III ran all over Vance Joseph's unit in the season opener, though it looks like he might do that to just about everyone. In Week 2, the Broncos completely blanked a very good Jaguars offense in the second half and stumped one of the best play-callers in the NFL in Liam Coen.

Now, the Denver defense faces arguably the biggest test in the entire NFL. The Rams have one of the most talented offenses in the league, and even if Puka Nacua isn't able to go because of his hip injury, the combination of Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay makes LA very difficult to stop.

The Broncos slowed down a Jags team that is known for running the ball effectively in Week 2, but they did so mostly by getting to Trevor Lawrence and winning the battle on passing downs. The Jags still had decent success running the ball, gaining 95 yards on 24 carries with an EPA just above zero.

That came on the heels of a Week 1 performance by Denver that was much more alarming in that area. The Chiefs ran for 220 yards with a +0.33 EPA per rush in that game per Next Gen Stats, so the jury is definitely still out on this Broncos run defense.

When you think about the Rams, you think about Stafford, Nacua and Davante Adams, but the running game is the foundation for what McVay wants to do with this offense.

That was on full display in Week 2 on Monday night. The Rams ran for 149 yards on 25 carries against the Giants, to the tune of a whopping +0.36 EPA per play. Both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are contributing on the ground, and the Rams' offensive line is able to get downhill and dominate in McVay's duo-heavy scheme. If they can do that, Stafford and the passing game will have a much easier time moving the ball as the Broncos pass rush won't be able to pin their ears back.

At the moment, it looks like Nacua is a longshot to play in this game. He was banged up all training camp with hip and groin issues, and didn't practice at all or play in Week 2. He has still yet to practice this week, so his status for Sunday night is looking bleak after McVay called it "doubtful" that he would be out there.

If Nacua doesn't go, that leaves the Rams with Davante Adams as the No. 1 receiver and a host of journeyman options behind him. That didn't hinder the Los Angeles passing attack on Monday night, as Adams reeled in eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. However, this Broncos secondary is a significantly more daunting challenge than the beat-up unit that the Giants rolled out there.

The Broncos love to play man coverage, and they have the personnel to do so with Patrick Surtain II on the outside. Surtain is arguably the best cornerback in all of football and can erase half of the field anytime he is out there.

This season, Denver has played man coverage on 35.9% of its defensive snaps, the sixth-highest number in the NFL according to Football Insights.

Of course, with Nacua likely out this week, Surtain can just follow Adams around all day. That will be especially limiting in the red zone, when the Rams love to get Adams isolated and ask him to win in one-on-one situations.

Behind Surtain, the Broncos still have a number of capable cornerbacks. Riley Moss has become underrated over the years despite being targeted at will, and Ja'Quan McMillian is a quality starter in the nickel.

Behind Adams, with Nacua out of the lineup, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield will all see more looks. Tight ends Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson will also have to step up in this game.

All of these secondary pieces for the Rams will have to make individual plays against the man coverage that the Broncos will throw at them, especially if Surtain is having success against Adams on the outside. Who wins that battle could determine who comes out on top under the lights in Denver on Sunday night.

title: Blazers news: NBA scout’s brutal ‘physically unfit’ Ja Morant assessment turns heads
description: An anonymous NBA scout delivered a brutal assessment of Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant ahead of training camp, calling the former All-Star “ physically unfit ” while raising concerns about his fit alongside Damian Lillard . “He’s got a bad knee, doesn’t really work on his physical fitness, I doubt that he’s all of a sudden become an […] The post Blazers news: NBA scout’s brutal ‘physically unfit’ Ja Morant assessment turns heads appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Blazers news: NBA scout's brutal 'physically unfit' Ja Morant assessment turns heads appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

An anonymous NBA scout delivered a brutal assessment of Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant ahead of training camp, calling the former All-Star "physically unfit" while raising concerns about his fit alongside Damian Lillard.

"He's got a bad knee, doesn't really work on his physical fitness, I doubt that he's all of a sudden become an elite-level shooter, and he's small," the scout told Sports Illustrated's Blake Silverman. "So you have that, you've got a bad defender who's a small guard who can't shoot, who physically is unfit, paired next to a small guard who's a bad defender and who can shoot [in Lillard]. So probably going to be tough."

The criticism comes as Morant prepares to open training camp next Tuesday with his new team after the Trail Blazers acquired the 27-year-old from the Memphis Grizzlies earlier this offseason.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The scout also questioned Morant's ability to stay on the floor consistently, although he suggested Portland could see more of the guard than Memphis did last season.

"We will probably see a more available Ja. He might play in games," the scout said.

Availability has become a significant concern for Morant in recent years. The former No. 2 overall pick has never appeared in more than 67 regular-season games in a single campaign, reaching that mark during his rookie season in 2019-20.

Morant appeared in only nine games during the 2023-24 season, although a 25-game suspension contributed to his limited availability. He followed that by playing 50 games in 2024-25 before appearing in just 20 games last season.

While the anonymous scout questioned whether Morant and Lillard can thrive together, former NBA head coach PJ Carlesimo recently offered a considerably more optimistic assessment of Portland's new backcourt.

Carlesimo told Kyle Odegard of NEXTPredict that he believes Lillard's basketball intelligence and willingness to adjust will help the Trail Blazers make the pairing work.

"I don't think there's any question," Carlesimo said. "Not that Ja is not capable of adjusting, but Dame is such a smart player. Dame will figure it out. Dame will do whatever it takes for the two of them to excel. And Dame will go out of his way to make sure Ja gets back to being Ja.

"Dame's game is so good and he's so smart. He will do whatever he needs to do to still be Dame, and yet at the same time, there's no bad ego there with Dame. He will make sure things work out for Ja."

Carlesimo also expressed hope that Morant can rediscover the form that made him a two-time All-Star early in his career.

"Some people forget, face of the league is what people were saying at that point," Carlesimo said. "Not a good player, a spectacular player. You loved to watch him play. I just hope he gets back to what he was, or even close, and plays the way Ja Morant can play."

Morant averaged 26.2 points, 8.1 assists and 5.9 rebounds per game during the 2022-23 season, his most recent All-Star campaign.

The contrasting assessments put additional attention on Morant as Portland prepares for training camp. His health, conditioning and ability to coexist with Lillard will be among the primary storylines surrounding the Trail Blazers as they prepare for the 2026-27 season.

title: Colts officially place WR Alec Pierce on IR and add wideout reinforcements to active roster
description: The Colts made an anticipated move at wideout regarding Alec Pierce, while adding receiving reinforcements to help with depth.
fullText:
The Indianapolis Colts announced on Saturday that wideout Alec Pierce, as expected and reported earlier in the week, has been placed on injured reserve—which means he'll miss at minimum, the team's next four games.

Having recently returned from his ankle/heel injury that cost him largely all of the offseason, Pierce re-injured the ankle/heel in the late first quarterback last Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs. He was unable to place his body weight on his latest injury and went to the medical blue tent along the sidelines, before being carted off the field. Pierce was seen post-game in a medical boot and on crutches within the player concourses.

Even though Pierce could theoretically return as soon as Week 6, the initial reports were that a return could realistically be closer to midseason, which could mean closer to Week 8 or 9 for Pierce's availability again.

Through two starts, Pierce has 5 receptions for 72 total receiving yards, having initially been on a pitch count—working his way back from the initial ankle/heel injury, which required minor cleanup offseason surgery.

As a potential Pierce interim replacement, the Colts promoted Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from their practice squad for Sunday and signed fellow wideout and special teams returnman Anthony Gould respectively.

As you may recall, the Colts signed wideout Nick Westbrook-Ikhine (6,'2", 211 pounds) as their original big bodied Michael Pittman Jr. possession wideout earlier this past offseason. Even though Westbrook-Ikhine flashed at times during training camp, the Colts ultimately signed veteran wideout Keenan Allen late in training camp, which made Westbrook-Ikhine's skill-set a bit redundant.

Westbrook-Ikhine became a roster casualty, as he was among the team's final 53-man roster cuts, before being re-signed to the team's practice squad. However, he was recently elevated and added to the active roster today for Sunday.

title: Jeremiah Smith ties Ohio State record with 4 TD catches as No. 7 Buckeyes beat Illinois 42-19
description: Smith's performance 23rd time since 2000 a FBS player has had double-digit catches for at least 200 yards and four scores in a game.
fullText:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — Jeremiah Smith tied an Ohio State record with four touchdown catches and also had career highs with 12 receptions for 217 yards as the seventh-ranked Buckeyes beat Illinois 42-19 on Saturday.

According to Sportradar, it is the 23rd time since 2000 a FBS player has had double-digit catches for at least 200 yards and four scores in a game. The last to do it was Western Michigan's Sky Moore against Northern Illinois in 2021.

It is the fifth time an Ohio State receiver has had four touchdowns. The last time it happened before Saturday was Noah Brown at Oklahoma in 2016.

It also tied for the sixth-most receiving yards in an OSU game and tied for sixth-most receptions.

Smith tied the mark with 10:07 remaining in the fourth quarter when he was wide open on a 26-yard touchdown to extend the Buckeyes' lead to 35-13.

Smith also became the third receiver since 2015 from a Power Four conference to have at least three games with at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns in one half. DeVonta Smith had four at Alabama and Ja'Marr Chase did it three times at LSU.

Julian Sayin completed 27 of 36 passes for 367 yards and added had a rushing TD as the Buckeyes (3-1, 1-0) opened Big Ten play with a victory for the 15th straight season.

Illinois (2-2, 0-1) kept it competitive despite Smith's monster game. Katin Houser was 21 of 37 passing for 263 yards and a touchdown and Jordan Anderson had a 22-yard rushing score in the first quarter.

Two plays after Sayin connected with Smith for a 31-yard completion to the Illinois 12 on the opening drive, Smith got leverage on Illini defensive back Juice Clark and hauled in a 7-yard TD to give the Buckeyes a score on their first possession for the third straight game.

After Illinois punted, Smith extended the lead to 14-0 with a 72-yard touchdown, the second-longest catch of his career.

On first-and-10 at the OSU 28, Sayin ran a go route down the middle of the field and got behind Mac Resetich. He caught it at the Illinois 27, did a double move at the 19 to get Resetich turned around in coverage and took it to the house.

The junior then had a highlight grab with 4:12 remaining in the second quarter to put Ohio State up 21-7. On first-and-goal at the 9, Smith got his left foot in near the corner of the end zone while being blanketed in coverage by Tywan Cox.

Illinois: Wide receiver Collin Dixon, who came into the game leading the nation with eight receiving touchdowns, was held to five catches for 63 yards.

Ohio State: Defense will be concern after the Illini rushed for 199 yards and averaged 6.0 yards per carry.

title: Tennessee football offense, Faizon Brandon stumble vs No. 1 Texas | Estes
description: Rapid reaction from 13th-ranked Tennessee’s 20-17 loss to top-ranked Texas before a checkered crowd at Neyland Stadium:
fullText:
KNOXVILLE – Rapid reaction from 13th-ranked Tennessee's 20-17 loss to top-ranked Texas before a checkered crowd at Neyland Stadium:

-In a stunning late sequence, Tennessee nearly overcame a 10-point deficit in the final 90 seconds. The Vols recovered an onside kick after scoring their first offensive touchdown with 1:22 remaining, but they weren't able to turn it into points. Faizon Brandon's Hail Mary pass fell incomplete in the end zone on the final play.

-Ultimately, strong defense and a punt-return touchdown weren't enough for Tennessee to overcome its inability to block Texas' defensive front. The Vols' offensive line was pushed around all game, resulting in a whopping 10 sacks, a lack of explosive plays and a quiet day on the ground. That last one was especially surprising, since Tennessee entered this game with one of the nation's best rushing attacks. Prior to that desperation TD drive by Tennessee's offense in the final minutes, it was averaging 1.5 yards per carry and 2.2 yards per play.

-Texas quarterback Arch Manning only threw 19 passes, but he completed 14 for 201 yards against an aggressive Tennessee defense that pressured him into six sacks and held the Longhorns' offense in check for much for this game. Manning did enough, though. With a 13-10 lead in the fourth quarter, he led an eight-play touchdown drive that ended up being the game-winning points.

-Brandon, the Vols' freshman quarterback, returned from a scary-looking injury in the first half to finish the game, though he appeared to be in pain during the final drive. After Brandon fell onto his right shoulder early while being tackled, sophomore backup George MacIntyre entered the game and threw three passes, completing one for 6 yards. Meanwhile, Brandon exited the injury tent and began throwing passes on the sideline before returning the game. The first play on his return? A quarterback run up the middle.

-Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons was a menace all game for Tennessee's offense, finishing with five sacks. Simmons, however, was also flagged for one of the dumbest, yet hilarious, penalties you'll ever see in the second quarter. After a sack of Brandon on third-and-13, which would've forced Tennessee to punt at its own 12-yard-line, Simmons instead gifted the Vols a first down when he celebrated by pretending to unzip his pants and urinate on the field. He was penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct, allowing the Vols to continue what ended up being a 15-play drive before it stalled without points at the Longhorns' 34.

After Qua Moss' punt return tied the game 10-10 in the third quarter, Texas replied with a 48-yard drive for a field goal to retake the lead. The key play was a 30-yard throw to Cam Coleman in which Manning withstood pressure (roughing the passer was called) to complete a pivotal pass on second-and-10, anyway, beating Ty Redmond in coverage.

1 – Number of offensive plays for Tennessee that gained 20 yards or more. And that was Brandon's TD throw to Mike Matthews in the game's final minutes. The longest gain of the first half was a 13-yard run, and the longest gain of the third quarter was an 18-yard pass.

This Tennessee defense might be for real. After allowing Texas' too-easy TD drive to open the game, Jim Knowles' unit responded and kept the Vols in this game all afternoon despite the offense's struggles. Manning rarely looked comfortable. He rarely had room to scramble, and the talented Longhorns couldn't get much going on the ground.

You expected that there would be freshman moments for Brandon. But this was an alarming afternoon for Tennessee's entire offense, and especially an O-Line that was exposed by the Longhorns' defensive front. Before, during and after Brandon's injury, it felt like nothing came easy for the Vols' offensively. Josh Heupel's teams won't often win big games when that's happening.

title: 'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final
description: Wakefield Trinity were playing in rugby league's second tier in 2024. Two years on, they are one win away from becoming Super League champions.
fullText:
"It's something I've dreamed about for years and it used to be a bit of a pipe dream," said Tom Johnstone, when asked about the prospect of Wakefield Trinity winning a Super League Grand Final.

That dream could become a reality for the England winger on 3 October, after Wakefield shocked treble-chasing Wigan Warriors 33-6 in Saturday's play-off semi-final to secure their place in the Old Trafford showpiece for the first time.

Wakefield, who will play Warrington Wolves in the title decider, have been a club transformed in recent seasons.

So often competing at the wrong end of the Super League table, they lost their top-flight status in 2023 - but that proved to be the beginning of the club's reinvigoration, sparked by the completion of a takeover by kitchen magnate Matt Ellis.

His financial support, along with the leadership and experience of head coach Daryl Powell, have led Wakefield up from the Championship and now to within 80 minutes of becoming Super League champions.

Johnstone, 31, began his career with Wakefield and was back for Trinity's return to the top division at the start of 2025 after a two-year spell with Catalans Dragons.

"I went to Matt's kitchen factory with my agent and we had a chat about everything they want to achieve and everything they promised to do," Johnstone, who scored two of Wakefield's five tries against Wigan, told BBC Two.

"We left and said: 'If they do any of that, it's going to be something special.' I couldn't say no."

Powell, who was appointed shortly after Wakefield had dropped into the second tier, added: "The journey's been an interesting one.

"We got relegated but it was probably good for us. It allowed us to stabilise the team, get our staff in and sign some players that got us out of the Championship.

"We started to sign high-quality players like Mike [McMeeken] and Tom, and some of the guys we signed the year before have really grown and prospered."

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Prior to the semi-final, many viewed Wakefield - who finished fourth in Super League - as second favourites against a Wigan team that had won 16 successive matches and were seeking a second domestic treble in the space of three seasons.

But Trinity responded brilliantly to falling behind early on and took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, seizing control of the contest and winning it with 33 unanswered points.

Ex-England half-back Kevin Brown, working as a BBC pundit, described Wakefield's display against Wigan as "definitely their best ever performance in Super League", adding: "It's been an incredible story where we're at right now and we're going to run out of superlatives if they go and win it."

Captain McMeeken has played in three previous Grand Finals with Castleford and Catalans, while he was also part of the England side that played in a World Cup semi-final on home soil in 2022 - but the significance of Saturday's achievement was not lost on him, either.

"To take in an experience like this is up there as one of the best moments of my career so far," he said.

At Old Trafford, Powell will come up against the club he coached for a season and a half before his exit midway through the 2023 campaign.

He said: "It's not about me or my journey, it's about the players and how they're writing different scripts every time we take the field."

Whoever is victorious will be a first-time Super League champion and Powell added: "It'll be awesome for the game. I think it's awesome that we're there in particular, Warrington have been there before.

"For us, it's about not getting too ahead of ourselves, playing the game as it is like we did tonight, and if we do that, we've got a great chance."

title: Man United’s financial woes deepen after move that makes a mockery of Ratcliffe’s “world’s most profitable club” claim
description: 1Manchester United’s debt has ballooned even further after the latest move by the club, a report has highlighted.Financial shapeEarlier this week, United released their latest financial results, con...
fullText:
Manchester United's debt has ballooned even further after the latest move by the club, a report has highlighted.

Earlier this week, United released their latest financial results, confirming an annual loss for the seventh successive year. United's combined losses since 2019 now stand at a staggering £444 million.

United posted a net loss of £43 million for 2025/26, which represents a significant increase on the £33 million for the previous 12 months.

Despite record revenue of £677.6 million, up 1.7% year on year, and a major cost-cutting drive under Sir Jim Ratcliffe that has seen hundreds of staff lose their jobs, United's losses have continued.

The Red Devils' wage bill dropped to £301 million, down 3.6% on the previous year, more than £100 million lower than cross-town rivals Manchester City, who were recently found guilty on 114 charges of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

Further details regarding United's financial results are available here.

According to the BBC, more information that was released by the club shows that United borrowed another £90 million since 30 June, piling on further debt.

During the summer transfer window, United secured the signings of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba for a combined £153 million.

But records show that United forked out £191.7 million on new players this summer. It's unclear where the extra sum was spent.

The BBC explain that United have been contacted for comment.

Simon Stone writes, "Confirmation of the additional borrowing of £90 million was included in a more detailed filing to the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, following Wednesday's release of their 2025-26 accounts to 30 June, and showed their overall debt was still more than £1 billion."

"United confirmed it made three further drawdowns from its revolving credit limit, on 29 and 31 July and 28 August, totalling £120 million. It then paid back £30 million on 21 September."

The 20-time English champions' overall debt has soared to £1.15 billion. This is made up of the historic debt the Glazers lumped on during their controversial leveraged buyout in 2005 (£578 million), the outstanding amount on the club's revolving credit facility (£200 million) and £375 million in outstanding transfer fees.

It's said that payments for most of United's recent transfers "are due within the next five years."

Certainly, Ratcliffe's assertion that United are now "the most profitable club in the world" rings hollow in light of these latest developments.

title: Dominant ground game powers Kentucky football past pesky South Alabama
description: Kentucky football's rushing attack excelled Saturday versus South Alabama. Three players went over 100 yards for the Wildcats in a 45-21 victory.
fullText:
LEXINGTON — Kentucky football's passing game never really got off the ground. UK's defense was stout at times and porous at others.

Good thing the Wildcats' rushing attack authored a game for the ages.

The dominance of Kentucky's running game powered it to a 45-21 victory over South Alabama on Saturday, Sept. 26, at Kroger Field.

All told, the Wildcats (3-1) rushed for 390 yards. Most impressively, they had three players run for 100 or more: CJ Baxter (149 yards on 16 carries), Jason Patterson (137 yards on 12 rushes) and Jovantae Barnes (100 yards on eight attempts).

It's the first time UK had a trio of 100-yard rushers in the same game since 2020, when Chris Rodriguez Jr., A.J. Rose and Terry Wilson did the honors versus Ole Miss. Kentucky had the benefit of overtime that day to pad stats.

It didn't need an extra period of play to accomplish the feat against South Alabama (2-2), though. After trailing 21-14, the Cats closed with a 31-0 flourish.

Of UK's tailback triumvirate, Patterson led the way in the scoring department, finding the end zone three times. Barnes and Baxter added one TD apiece.

It continued Baxter's torrid start to the season, up to five rushing TDs in four games. For Barnes, it marked his first score as a member of the Wildcats. The pair transferred into the program prior to this season, Barnes from Oklahoma and Baxter from Texas.

Patterson, on the other hand, never left. He remained at Kentucky in the transition from Mark Stoops to Will Stein.

While Barnes, Baxter and Patterson traversed separate paths to Lexington, their journeys have converged.

Those roads led to victory Saturday.

title: Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final
description: Wakefield Trinity produce a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.
fullText:
Betfred Super League play-off semi-final

Tries: Johnstone 2, Sinfield, Hall, Rodwell Goals: Jowitt 6 Drop-goal: Lino

Wakefield Trinity produced a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.

Having led 8-6 at the end of a tight first period, the visitors took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, with Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall all crossing while the Wigan centre was in the sin-bin.

England winger Johnstone had earlier replied to Brad O'Neill's opener for the Warriors and Ky Rodwell added Wakefield's fifth try as Trinity registered 33 unanswered points to book their spot at Old Trafford.

A Championship side as recently as 2024, Wakefield have made huge progress in recent seasons under ambitious owner Matt Ellis and experienced head coach Daryl Powell - and they are now just one win away from becoming Super League champions.

They will face Warrington Wolves in the title decider on Saturday, 3 October.

Wigan went into the play-off semi-final on a 16-game winning run and with two trophies - the Challenge Cup and the League Leaders' Shield - already secured.

However, their hopes of getting to a fourth consecutive Grand Final were crushed on home soil by an outstanding Wakefield display.

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final

Relive Wakefield's semi-final win over Wigan

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Wigan's only points came while Wakefield forward Jezz Tevaga was in the sin-bin for a trip on Liam Marshall, but it was Keighran's yellow card for a late tackle on Isaiah Vagana that proved to be the pivotal moment.

Wakefield's lead stretched from two points to 18 during Keighran's spell off the field, much to the delight of the away supporters stationed behind the end they were attacking.

Mason Lino's drop-goal and Max Jowitt's second penalty of the match added further gloss to the scoreline, and owner Ellis joined the celebrations on the field at full-time.

Only five clubs have won Grand Finals since the first was staged in 1998; Wigan, St Helens, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos and Hull KR.

Wakefield's win guarantees there will be a sixth name on the trophy and a new champion for the second successive year, following Rovers' victory in 2025.

Warrington have lost all four previous Grand Finals in which they have appeared, the most recent of them in 2018.

Powell, who was in charge of Castleford Tigers when they lost the Grand Final in 2017, is sure to be a central figure in the build-up, given his unspectacular season-and-a-half spell in charge of the Wolves which ended midway through the 2023 campaign.

Meanwhile, try-scoring half-back Sinfield is set to play in a Grand Final 11 years after his father, Sir Kevin Sinfield, made the last of his eight Grand Final appearances.

Sir Kevin won seven titles with Leeds Rhinos and he is scheduled to deliver the match ball before next Saturday's game to round off his latest fundraising effort for motor neurone disease (MND) charities.

"Hopefully he'll be there!" Jack Sinfield told BBC Two. "He's not here tonight because he's starting in the morning, but I'm sure he'll be watching and I can't wait to see him next week.

"I've been there [to Grand Finals] a fair few times watching so it will be nice to do it the other way round and he can hopefully watch me win one."

Interchanges: Farrell, Walters, Mago, Kerr.

Wakefield: Jowitt; Johnstone, Hall, Scott, Walmsley; Trueman, Sinfield; McMeeken, Smoothy, Rodwell, Lipowicz, Vagana, Tevaga.

Interchanges: Lino, Pitts, Hamlin-Uele, Faatili.

title: Mike Locksley contract buyout: How much would it cost to fire Maryland coach?
description: Mike Locksley's seat is hot after Maryland had another poor performance against UCLA on Saturday that came with plenty of boos.
fullText:
The hot seat is getting hotter for Mike Locksley.

Maryland football's struggles continued against UCLA, trailing to the Bruins 34-3 at the end of third quarter. The boo birds were already out in the first half for what crowd made it out to SECU Stadium.

The likely loss is just latest low for Maryland as there have been increasing concerns about the direction of the program. Locksley's job security was already getting murkier after back-to-back 4-8 seasons. Now Maryland is on its way to 2-2, with two losses before the end of September for the first time since Locksley's first season in 2019.

Going back to last season, the Terrapins will have lost 10 of their past 12 games, and things don't look like they're going to get better as Big Ten play begins, and Terp fans are wondering how long it will take until Maryland officially starts the search for a new coach.

Locksley's buyout at Maryland would amount to $9.2 million if the university fired him without cause on or before Dec. 31, 2026, according to a copy of his contract obtained via USA TODAY Sports.

The Maryland coach receives $6.4 million this season, with pay is split up into $600,000 in base pay and $5.8 million in supplemental compensation.

His contract, which runs through the end of the 2028 season, is set for increased pay with his salary at $6.7 million for 2027 and $7 million for 2028.

If fired, he is owed 65% of his salary.

title: Pitt's Mason Heintschel Makes ACC History With Another Six-TD Game
description: Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to throw for at least six touchdowns in multiple games in the same season after another record-setting performance.
fullText:
Pitt's Mason Heintschel Makes ACC History With Another Six-TD Game originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh. Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel is making history during a record-setting sophomore season.

Heintschel became the first quarterback in ACC history to throw for at least six touchdowns in multiple games in the same season after tossing six touchdown passes in Pitt's 59-0 win over Bucknell on Saturday.

The performance marked Heintschel's second six-touchdown game of the season. He opened the year by throwing seven touchdown passes against Miami (Ohio), breaking the ACC's single-game record for touchdown passes.

Pitt's Mason Heintschel is the first player in ACC history to throw for 6+ TDs in multiple games in the same season‼️ He's the first FBS player to do so since 2021 (C.J. Stroud and Bailey Zappe). He's only the second player in ACC history to have multiple such games in a career, joining Deshaun Watson who did so in 2014 and 2016 🏈

Heintschel is also the first FBS quarterback to record multiple games with at least six touchdown passes in a season since 2021, when C.J. Stroud and Bailey Zappe each accomplished the feat.

His latest performance also put him in rare ACC company. Clemson's Deshaun Watson is the only other ACC quarterback to record multiple games with at least six touchdown passes in his career, doing so in 2014 and 2016.

Heintschel finished Saturday's game 29-of-37 passing for 403 yards, six touchdowns and no interceptions. He also added 33 rushing yards on three carries before giving way to backup Holden Geriner midway through the third quarter.

Final stat line for @mason_heinch06 ⬇️

29-37, 403 yards, 6 TDs pic.twitter.com/HYR6GtNuUE

Three of Heintschel's touchdown passes went to Censere Lee, while Demetrice McCray caught two and Carson Kent caught one.

The performance came as a bounce-back for Heintschel, who had struggled during Pitt's previous two games against UCF and Syracuse. He completed 28 of 52 passes for 335 yards with no touchdown passes and one interception across those contests.

Heintschel's resurgence helped Pitt put together a historic offensive performance of its own. The Panthers totaled 766 yards, including a program-record 574 passing yards. Pitt's eight total passing touchdowns also tied an ACC single-game record.

The Panthers improved to 4-0 with the victory and completed their second undefeated nonconference schedule in program history.

Now, Heintschel and the Panthers turn their attention to ACC play. Pitt's first conference game comes Friday night on the road against Virginia Tech, which also enters the matchup at 4-0.

title: Steelers Place Promising Rookie on Injured Reserve
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have placed rookie guard Gennings Dunker on the injured reserve list, the team announced on Saturday. According […]
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have placed rookie guard Gennings Dunker on the injured reserve list, the team announced on Saturday.

According to report by Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Dunker suffered an MCL sprain when he got his leg rolled up on at practice on Thursday, and he is expected to miss four to six weeks, but will not have to have surgery. Dunker did not practice on Friday and had already been ruled out for this week's AFC North-opening contest against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Fellow guard Spencer Anderson, who started the Steelers' initial two games to Zach Frazier's right, reportedly suffered a broken bone in his lower right leg during Sunday's loss to the New England Patriots. Anderson was a full participant in practice all week, but Brock Hoffman seems likely to start in his place on Sunday in any case.

Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was sacked four times in that loss, including one where Patriots linebacker Christian Elliss zoomed in off the left edge and hit the 42-year-old in his back at full speed.

Dunker, an Iowa product, was tabbed as an inactive for the Steelers' first two games. He was among the blockers that Steelers offensive line coach James Campen praised for his progress since arriving in black and gold.

Dunker, who stands at 6-foot-5, 319 pounds, has 33.5-inch arms and 10-inch hands. He played both left guard and right tackle at Iowa. He's an absolute mauler in the run game, but needs to improve in the pass blocking department.

Dunker played through multiple injuries in the 2025 season (shoulder, MCL tear). His toughness and grit are two traits that were praised by analysts in the pre-draft process.

He made headlines at the NFL Combine for his flowing red-haired mullet and thick mustache. Dunker is widely known for his love of Culver's, a Midwestern fast-food chain.

Former Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro center Jason Kelce said after Dunker was drafted that he has the exact physique desired from a big man on the offensive side of the ball.

"He looks like a Clydesdale," Kelce said. "If you were gonna design an offensive lineman in a laboratory, this is what he'd look like."

Chris Ward and Brendan Howe contributed.

title: Here we go, Liverpool about to sign Andoni Iraola's 'new' Eli Junior Kroupi
description: Andoni Iraola will soon have his next Eli Junior Kroupi at Anfield. The Spanish coach is very much settling into life at Liverpool. Iraola's philosophy is still taking time to be instilled in his new ...
fullText:
Andoni Iraola will soon have his next Eli Junior Kroupi at Anfield.

The Spanish coach is very much settling into life at Liverpool. Iraola's philosophy is still taking time to be instilled in his new team. He's also getting to know his players and the culture around the club.

It's good to see how positive Iraola has been. He's open to working with younger players, has already done a tremendous job promoting Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni and he wants to play progressive attacking football.

The intensity has been back. Liverpool are pressing with greater force and covering more distances than they were under Arne Slot.

Most importantly, Iraola is embedding himself into the culture of the club. This weekend, he's set to attend Liverpool's Women game against Everton.

So, he's getting involved at all levels of the club, which is a very exciting change compared to Slot, who would use these international breaks to go on holiday to Ibiza.

Naturally, Iraola is definitely a lot 

However, if Liverpool are to be successful, he still needs a few missing pieces from his arsenal.

At Bournemouth, Iraola used a different type of no.10 to Florian Wirtz. He often played Eli Junior Kroupi in the role, who is more of a false nine or forward, capable of scoring goals.

At Liverpool, Iraola doesn't really have this Kroupi profile, but he may soon.

Anfield Watch understands Liverpool's scouts are huge admirers of the German U21 international who has scored six goals for AS Monaco already this season.

Brunner is someone who Liverpool's scouts have watched in person several times already this season. Now this only happens when the club is seriously interested in a player.

Naturally, Liverpool will be keeping a close eye on his teammate Lamine Camara as well. But Brunner is held in high regard and he is a serious target in order to provide competition for the no.10 role.

That means Liverpool are very much considering signing him and in the process, they could be about to bring in Iraola's very own Kroupi.

Brunner is a similar profile to the Frenchman. He positions himself in similar positions and he is the type of supporting striker/no.10 who prefers to score goals and arrive in the box, as well as link-up with his teammates.

title: Kevin Colbert Opens Up About His ‘Special’ 22-Year Run With the Steelers
description: It’s a season of many congratulations for former Pittsburgh Steelers GM Kevin Colbert as the franchise inducts him into the Hall of Honor. His stint with the Steelers oversaw some of the most incredible years in the club’s history, and his contributions are now getting the nearly inevitable applause they deserve. ​Colbert spent 22 years […] The post Kevin Colbert Opens Up About His ‘Special’ 22-Year Run With the Steelers appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
It's a season of many congratulations for former Pittsburgh Steelers GM Kevin Colbert as the franchise inducts him into the Hall of Honor. His stint with the Steelers oversaw some of the most incredible years in the club's history, and his contributions are now getting the nearly inevitable applause they deserve.

​Colbert spent 22 years in the organization's front office, during which the former GM made notable moves in building the team into a formidable side. Those years saw him and the team build two Super Bowl championship teams alongside one of the best eras in the Steelers' history. It's all nostalgia and more for Colbert, who grew up on the streets of Pittsburgh, as he joins an elite list of franchise heroes.

Colbert received widespread congratulations from different high-profile administrators, including head coach Mike Tomlin, who were part of Colbert's Steelers story. One of Colbert's most notable moves involved drafting Ben Roethlisberger in 2004, a choice that helped define the squad for years. In all, he built something special in Pittsburgh, and his fingerprints are all over the Steelers' success.

"We were able to be part of the six Super Bowls, and that's always going to be a special memory. But in all honesty, being a part of this organization and the greatness that the organization always is, the standard that they've always held. It's the realization of how special it was and how fortunate I was, and my family was, to be part of such a great organization and a great family of players, coaches, administrators, staff. Just to be a part of that. That's always going to be the special moment, even though it was a 22-year moment."​

Former Steelers GM Kevin Colbert at the 2026 Hall of Honor Dinner on being apart of the organization: “We were able to be part of the six Super Bowls and that's always going to be a special memory. But in all honesty, being a part of this organization and the greatness that the…

— Steelers Depot 7⃣ (@Steelersdepot) September 26, 2026

Colbert worked with the front office for a full 22 years, from 2000 to 2022, across auto roles. During that period, he helped to assemble two Super Bowl championship teams, Super Bowl 40 and Super Bowl 43.

The 69-year-old has come out publicly to reveal some of the behind-the-scenes of his famous choices. For instance, during an episode of the Inside the Game podcast this year, Colbert walked listeners through how the franchise, picking 11th, somehow managed to get Roethlisberger's signature.

​Such decision-making processes characterized Colbert's run. Over his 22 years, the Steelers went 226-124-3 in the regular season and won the AFC North ten times. That period also saw them make the playoffs 14 times. These numbers show why Colbert, alongside other honorees, former defensive back J.T. Thomas and longtime player-turned-commentator Craig Wolfley, joined the Steelers' Hall of Honor Class of 2026.

​Former first-round pick Thomas was a part of four Super Bowl-winning squads, playing for the Steelers from 1973 through 1981. His late interception of Raiders quarterback Ken Stabler in the 1974 AFC Championship sealed the triumph that earned the Steelers their first Super Bowl appearance.

​Wolfley was a 1980 fifth-round pick who spent 10 seasons with the Steelers as a guard and tackle. He featured in 129 regular-season games, with 102 starts for the Steelers. Wolfley passed in 2025. The class was officially inducted on Friday night at a dinner at Acrisure Stadium. All three will be celebrated again on Sunday when the Steelers take on the Cincinnati Bengals.

title: Julian Ward needs to recreate his biggest success at Anfield
description: Julian Ward has been officially announced as Liverpool’s new sporting director. The Englishman will replace Richard Hughes, who departed at the end of the summer, and is returning to a role he held ...
fullText:
Julian Ward has been officially announced as Liverpool's new sporting director.

The Englishman will replace Richard Hughes, who departed at the end of the summer, and is returning to a role he held during the 2022-23 season.

Ward is extending a 14-year affiliation with the Reds, and is one of the most experienced in his profession, especially when it comes to Liverpool.

There are some obvious challenges awaiting the new sporting director, but not all of them can be fixed in the transfer market and many supporters will be hoping he can recreate a big success from his last stint at Anfield.

Although Liverpool's new sporting director is remembered fondly for the signings he made, including Alexis Mac Allister, Luis Diaz and Cody Gakpo, one of his greatest successes actually came in negotiations with Mohamed Salah.

In July 2022, early in Ward's first reign as sporting director, Salah penned a contract extension at Anfield and the deal was viewed as one of the most important bits of business Liverpool undertook that summer.

Now the Reds find themselves in a position where some of their most important players are into the final 12 months of their deals, having already lost Andrew Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Salah for free this summer.

The two most important contracts to address are those of Alisson Becker and Virgil van Dijk.

The pair have been absolutely crucial to Liverpool's success over the last decade and losing both in the same summer for nothing would be a huge blow.

Although 35 and 33 respectively, Van Dijk and Alisson are still performing at the very highest level and have much more to offer the Reds.

Even if an extension only sees them stay until the summer of 2027, keeping both Van Dijk and Alisson in Merseyside would be one of the best bits of business Ward could do.

Ward has done it before with Salah, now it is time to extend two of Liverpool's bets players once again.

title: Detroit Red Wings add scrappy defenseman who loves to drop the gloves
description: The Detroit Red Wings have claimed defenseman Andreas Englund off waivers, adding some toughness to their organizational depth.
fullText:
The Detroit Red Wings claimed defenseman Andreas Englund off waivers, adding to their organizational depth.

The transaction on Saturday, Sept. 26 came hours before the Wings' final exhibition game, and two days before the 5 p.m. deadline to trim rosters to 23 players.

The 6-foot-4, 200-pound Englund, 30, appeared in three games (no points) last season with the Nashville Predators and has 200 career NHL games (20 points, minus-26 rating) on his resume, with a journeyman's list of stops also including the Ottawa Senators, Colorado Avalanche, Chicago Blackhawks and Los Angeles Kings.

He's stood out in his career for his scrappiness, picking up 190 penalty minutes, including 24 fights, most notably 11 during the 2023-24 season.

MORE: Why the battle to make Detroit Red Wings' defense is so heated

Englund, originally the 40th overall selection by the Senators in the 2014 draft, was signed in the offseason by the Calgary Flames to a one-year, two-way contract for $900,000. The Flames placed him on waivers Friday.

The Wings entered Saturday's game against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Little Caesars Arena with eight defensemen on their roster, plus Simon Edvinsson, who is unsigned: Moritz Seider, Ben Chiarot, Justin Faulk, Albert Johansson, Axel Sandin-Pellikka, Jacob Bernard-Docker, Anton Johansson and William Wallinder. Edvinsson has been practicing with the team but remains in need of a new contract.

title: 49ers’ Jordan Watkins Set for Bigger Opportunity as Kyle Shanahan Explains His Early Absence
description: The San Francisco 49ers are 2-0, however, their wide receiver room is getting thinner by the week. Injuries have already changed the mix, forcing the 49ers to lean harder on players who weren’t expected to carry major roles this early. fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers are 2-0, however, their wide receiver room is getting thinner by the week. Injuries have already changed the mix, forcing the 49ers to lean harder on players who weren't expected to carry major roles this early. That has also created a different look at the depth chart, with several young receivers now sitting closer to meaningful opportunities.

One of those players is Jordan Watkins. The former Ole Miss standout has spent the opening weeks waiting for his chance; however, the situation around him has changed quickly, with another receiver now unavailable. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has offered some insight into why Watkins has been waiting and what could come next.

On September 26, Shanahan said Watkins is now in line for an opportunity after spending the first two games inactive. Shanahan made it clear that Watkins's absence was not solely due to his work as a receiver.

"He's gonna have an opportunity now….I think he's gotten a lot better in a lot of facets. You know I think him not being up in these last couple games has been more on because of special teams than a receiver deal. If it were just on receiver base and things like that I think he would have got up Week 1."

Kyle Shanahan on Jordan Watkins:

“He’s gonna have an opportunity now….I think he’s gotten a lot better in a lot of facets. You know I think him not being up in these last couple games has been more on because of special teams than a receiver deal. If it were just on receiver… pic.twitter.com/TXxNshb7JL

— OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) September 25, 2026

That distinction matters. Watkins was not necessarily being held back because the Niners disliked what he was doing at wide receiver. Shanahan pointed instead to the special-teams side of the roster decision, suggesting Watkins could have been active earlier if the decision had been based strictly on his development as a pass catcher.

Demarcus Robinson has been ruled out after suffering an ankle injury against the Miami Dolphins last week. He had already shown some value in Shanahan's offense, opening the season with two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams before adding three receptions for 34 yards against the Dolphins.

Robinson's absence gives Watkins a path onto the active roster and potentially into the offensive rotation. That opportunity comes at a time when the 49ers' receiver depth has already taken several hits. Ricky Pearsall is out for the season after knee surgery, while De'Zhaun Stribling is on injured reserve.

Watkins has also given the coaching staff something to work with. During the preseason, he caught 13 passes for 164 yards and a touchdown, showing enough progress to remain in the conversation despite his limited early-season role.

That fight could finally turn into snaps. The 49ers recently added veteran Brandin Cooks as another option, so Watkins still has competition around him; however, with Robinson unavailable and injuries reshaping the room, the former Ole Miss receiver now has the opening he has been waiting for.

title: Dak Prescott Brushes Off Concerns Over Cowboys’ Playing Surface in Brazil
description: The Dallas Cowboys quarterback has often shown a nonchalant attitude toward many aspects of the game. He again showed that attitude as the Cowboys prepared for their Week 3 game against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. ​The Cowboys arrived in Brazil ahead of the game, practicing at the Rio de Janeiro stadium to get a […] The post Dak Prescott Brushes Off Concerns Over Cowboys’ Playing Surface in Brazil appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys quarterback has often shown a nonchalant attitude toward many aspects of the game. He again showed that attitude as the Cowboys prepared for their Week 3 game against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil.

​The Cowboys arrived in Brazil ahead of the game, practicing at the Rio de Janeiro stadium to get a feel for the environment ahead of the international NFL game. Since their arrival, discussions have grown concerning the state of the pitch, as many criticized its suitability for the football game. Dak Prescott would rather focus on what he can control.

Maracanã Stadium, where the game will be held, has drawn criticism from soccer players for poor playing conditions. The league has reinforced its choice of the stadium amid concerns that players are intentionally quiet on the topic. Prescott would not shy away from his views when the pressmen asked for his thoughts on the pitch. Jon Machota, a reporter for The Athletic, shares Prescott's comments during the media briefing via X.

​"Not a lot goes into that for me. I trust my equipment, the cleats that I'm going to have. Not really even looking into the news about how people feel about the field.​

"If it's the surface we're gonna play on, let's go do it. One way or another, obviously if they're gonna allow the game to be played, it's good enough. Where I'm from, I've played on worse. I've been tackled on concrete. So, the fact that the grass is soft, we'll take it. I'll take it anyways. I hope not to hit it anyways.​"

Cowboys QB Dak Prescott doesn’t seem too concerned about possible issues with the playing surface Sunday in Brazil: “Not a lot goes into that for me. I trust my equipment, the cleats that I’m going to have. Not really even looking into the news about how people feel about the… pic.twitter.com/6Q0SiEfBxY

— Jon Machota (@jonmachota) September 25, 2026

​Entering the game, Prescott has completed 73.8% of his passes for 454 yards and 6 touchdowns to 1 interception this season. Those numbers tie him ahead in the league in touchdown passes.

​If anything, many consider Prescott a fierce competitor who would not mind playing anywhere or anytime. He seemingly exudes the aura of an NFL player who is hardly fazed by much. That leaves no surprise regarding his comments on the pitch ahead of Sunday's tie.

​Several other athletes from the Cowboys and Ravens have spoken similarly on the pitch. Administrative professionals have also added their voice in support of the league's insistence on using the pitch. The players reportedly trust the league to ensure their adequate care.

Given Prescott's history of lower-leg injuries, his safety is worth weighing ahead of any game. Many expect each squad and other members of the NFL Players Association to keep an eye on the situation going into the game.

Until otherwise proven, Prescott chooses to align with the league's decision. Instead, he is focusing on getting ready to play following a decent Week 2 outing by throwing the football. His running game hasn't been as spectacular as his other traits. Many fans hoped he could build a significant rhythm with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens early in the game to provide a decent outing for the Cowboys and advance their 1-1 record after two games.

title: Detroit Lions place S Thomas Harper on IR, elevate 2 defenders for Week 3
description: The Detroit Lions make three roster moves ahead of their Week 3 game against the New York Jets.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions' injury woes at safety continue to worsen, as they announced Saturday that they placed safety Thomas Harper on injured reserve. Additionally, the Lions announced the elevation of two defensive players for their Week 3 game against the New York Jets, giving the unit more depth for the game.

Harper finished the Lions game against the Bills in Week 2, but suffered an ankle injury that required a walking boot. When practices began on Wednesday, Harper still needed the walking boot for support, but told Detroit News' Rich Silva that he was "just trying to stay off of it" and that it "shouldn't be (a) long-term" injury. Things were apparently more significant than Harper anticipated because he couldn't practice the rest of the week, was ruled out for Week 3 on Friday, and was placed on IR on Saturday. Harper will be required to miss the next four weeks and will not be eligible to return to the roster until Week 7, at the earliest.

Avonte Maddox was also placed on injured reserve this week—his injury will require surgery and is season-ending—and Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, meaning that the Lions are now down four of their top five options at safety.

So what's the plan moving forward?

For Week 3, the Lions will shift Christian Izen from his starting nickel role to a starting safety role, lining up opposite veteran Chuck Clark.

"Izzy's been working a lot back there and had a full week. And he's gotten a ton of work and this week a ton of reps, full-speed reps," Campbell said on Friday. "'This is what you're going to do, these are the calls,' and just dousing him with full-speed reps, and he's done a good job this week. […] Izzy's going to be a huge part for us."

As for their reserve roles, the Lions have three potential options, the most immediate being the game elevation of veteran safety Jalen Mills. Earlier this week, Mills re-signed with the Lions' practice squad to bolster the team's depth at safety. Mills is entering his 11th season in the NFL and spent time on the Lions roster late last season, playing in three games down the stretch. His familiarity with the defensive coverage scheme should help him get up to speed quickly and provide an immediate role against the Jets in Week 3.

The Lions' next option is rookie corner Keith Abney, who was getting "sprinkles back there a little bit as a reserve," according to Campbell. While he's primarily played nickel in Detroit, Abney has the intelligence and ability to work at safety in a pinch.

"For a rookie, he's a pretty dang smart, conscientious, aware football player that's got a ton of room to really take off," Campbell said of Abney on Friday. "So, that's a good sign. […] He just needs reps and reps. But if we need it, that'll be a guy who may have to go in for us."

Lastly, the Lions also poached rookie Bishop Fitzgerald off the Steelers' practice squad earlier in the week, and while he's surely not versed enough in the playbook to get meaningful snaps right now, he'll be an option in their safety depth moving forward. Fitzgerald is an ideal free safety in the Lions scheme because he can ballhawk from center field and be a willing tackler in run support. He'll need time to acclimate, but he has plus developmental upside.

In addition to Mills, the Lions also elevated linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga from the practice squad for this game. With rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder slowly returning from a hamstring injury and Joe Bachie recently released from the active roster, Ogbongbemiga will provide the Lions with LB6 depth and a role on multiple phases of special teams.

title: Stamford football doubles last season's win total with dominant win over Bridgeport Central
description: Anthony Evanko scored and had three sacks and an interception in Stamford's second straight win.
fullText:
STAMFORD - The Stamford football team needed just three games this season to double last season's win total as the Black Knights dominated Bridgeport Central 39-6 on Saturday to improve to 2-1 on the year.

"I told the kids last week, 'If you think 1-1 feels good, let's get to 2-1 and see how that feels,'" Stamford coach Donny Panapada said. "We are working hard. Opening against Danbury was a tough game for us, but I thought we played well. The last two weeks we did what we had to do and now we have a tough game next Friday against Stratford, our first road game, and we will prepare and we are looking forward to it."

Stamford will be at Stratford on Friday at 6 p.m., while Central will be at Bassick on Friday at 4 p.m.

Both teams were coming off wins: Stamford had beaten Bassick 41-0, and Central had beaten Wilby 35-0.

Stamford led 33-0 at halftime and held Central scoreless until the final 10 seconds of the game.

"Our defense was flying around," Panapada said. "We thought in this weather they would struggle throwing the ball so we played a lot of guys up at the line of scrimmage. They have some athletes that can break plays and we contained them, and it was nice to see."

Stamford got a 3-yard touchdown run by Dylan Depree, a 1-yard run by Anthony Evanko, a 1-yard run by Isaiah Stephens, who also caught a 3-yard touchdown pass from Jack Healy, a 24-yard pass from Healy to Malcolm Barrot, and a fumble recovery in the end zone by Xavier Perryman.

"It feels great to be 2-1 after last year and year before that," Evanko said. "We had high expectations coming into this game and everyone's energy was through the roof. Our team morale was incredible and we were having so much fun. This is the best football we have played in a long time."

Central's Ja'Khi Weatherford scored on a 19-yard run in the closing seconds to avoid the shutout.

Anthony Evanko, Stamford: In addition to his touchdown dive, the senior linebacker had three sacks and an interception for the Black Knights.

"Anthony is a very good football player. We are lucky enough to have a lot of kids who are like Anthony Evanko. It's a fun group to be around and we have to keep this thing rolling." - Stamford coach Donny Panapada.

fullText:
The Chicago Bears and the Philadelphia Eagles meet up on Monday Night Football, and each team has revealed its final injury report for the game. As expected, the Bears will be without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, but the door is open for Tyson Bagent.

Bagent entered concussion protocol earlier this week, but today he advanced enough to be able to get on the field and practice in a limited capacity. He's officially listed as questionable, and if he's cleared, he could dress on Monday night. Case Keenum still seems likely to get the start, but the Bears have a walk-through tomorrow, and all day Monday, so there's time.

Kicker Cairo Santos missed practice on Thursday and Friday with a hip injury, but was back today and has no injury designation. Also free of a designation is cornerback Tyroque Stevenson, who missed some time earlier this week with a hamstring issue.

As for Ozzy Trapilo, who has practiced in full for a second consecutive week, head coach Ben Johnson was asked if he'd be an option to start at left tackle on Monday night, and he said, "No." We'll know 90 minutes before kickoff if he's active, and being active in a game or two for some game reps would be a precursor to him taking over as the starter.

The Eagles will be without starting tight end Dallas Goedert, reserve receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown, and backup offensive tackle Fred Johnson.

Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard is questionable with a knee injury that limited him all week.

Running back Saquon Barkley, who was limited earlier in the week with a stinger, is not listed at all. Wideout DeVonta Smith also has no injury designation after missing Thursday's practice with a hamstring issue. Both practiced in full today.

fullText:
In President Donald Trump's latest move to restrict certain news outlets' access, CNN was not permitted to join the president on Air Force One on Saturday, Sept. 26, as he traveled to a football game at the University of Tennessee.

"I want real news. I love an open, free press," Trump said Saturday morning to reporters when asked about the decision to bar CNN. "What I don't like is the fake press, where a group like CNN, with few people watching, or MSDNC," the name that he calls MS NOW, formerly MSNBC.

CNN anchor Anderson Cooper announced the news about the Air Force One decision on his show Friday night. CNN was slated to cover Trump on Saturday on behalf of the television pool – where ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and FOX take turns covering Trump and sharing camera feeds with the other networks. CNN White House correspondent Alayna Treene explained to Cooper that the White House's guidance for the next day was released and that CNN was not included on the list of outlets traveling with Trump.

"The White House is barring CNN from flying on Air Force One on Saturday as part of the news outlet’s duties covering the president on behalf of major television networks," CNN Chief White House Correspondent Kaitlan Collins said in a post on X.

The latest action comes amid a legal dispute after the president attempted to block three news outlets – CNN, MS NOW and Politico – from the White House. Here's the timeline:

Trump spent his morning doubling down on his ban, saying in a Truth Social post that "FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE!!! IT HAS GONE ON FAR TOO LONG, AT A TREMENDOUS COST TO OUR COUNTRY."

"Why should perpetrators of FAKE NEWS, like CNN and MSDNC, be allowed access to a very sacred place, the White House? Despite my big Election Win, almost 100% of “TRUMP” coverage is negative, and has been for years," Trump said in a second Sept. 26 post.

fullText:
Four Americans were among the six people who died after an explosion and building collapse in Athens' tourist district of Plaka near the Acropolis on Friday, officials said.

A U.S. State Department spokesperson confirmed to CBS News on Saturday that their deaths were a result of a gas explosion.

"I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of four American citizens in yesterday's explosion in central Athens," Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to the Hellenic Republic, said on X.

"I extend my deepest appreciation to the Greek first responders who worked tirelessly at the scene. The U.S. Embassy is providing consular assistance and support to the victims' families."

The two other people killed were an elderly British man and his Greek wife who lived on the second floor of the three-story building, Greece's state broadcaster ERT reported.

The American family of four had been renting an apartment on the first floor and were preparing to go to the airport hours later Friday for their return to the United States when the blast occurred, according to the Kathimerini newspaper.

The explosion brought down the residential building and damaged properties and vehicles along the street. Two other women were injured from an adjacent building on Lysikratous Street, fire brigades said, according to the Associated Press.

The New York Times reported that the U.S. family was composed of a couple, their son and his girlfriend. Greek authorities did not immediately give their identities, ages or where in the U.S. they came from.

On Saturday, AFP reporters saw mechanical diggers moving debris at the site and thermal-imaging cameras deployed.

"We are talking about an incredible disaster," Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said.

Two nearby buildings were left in a dangerous state, he added, with inspections underway "to determine if they can remain standing or if they also have to be demolished."

The owner of the ground-floor apartment, Mathaios Artavanis, told the Kathimerini daily he was absent at the time of the blast. He said he had tried afterward to contact the U.K.-Greek couple who lived there, without success.

Video footage from the scene showed rubble strewn across the street, with parked cars smashed by falling debris. The people rescued by the fire department from the adjacent building were all tourists, resident Andreas Martzaklis said.

The pastor of a nearby church said this Sunday's service would be held outdoors because of damage to the church.

A year ago, locals in the Plaka neighborhood had warned the city and utility companies about the risk of gas leaks or short circuits, according to a letter by the residents' association published by Kathimerini.

The residents had urged a fire drill to identify possible weaknesses in the emergency response plans for the district.

A citizens' group said on social media that one resident in the street where the explosion happened had alerted authorities after smelling a possible gas leak.

The neighborhood is one of Athens' most popular tourist areas. The nearby Acropolis, one of Greece's best-known landmarks, welcomed 4.6 million visitors last year.
